description: Data model + pure BMI library foundation. Extend ProfilingAnswers with MANDATORY heightCm/weightKg, create the framework-free src/lib/bmi.ts (compute, Asia-Pacific category, bounds + validator), add its unit tests, and update EVERY existing ProfilingAnswers construction site so the strict types stay satisfied and the baseline 155 tests keep passing. This feature is the dependency root for FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: In src/types/index.ts, add two MANDATORY (non-optional) fields to the ProfilingAnswers interface: `heightCm: number` and `weightKg: number`. Keep the existing optional fields `lastMealHour?` and `wakeHour?`. Place a short comment noting Asia-Pacific BMI usage.

Create src/lib/bmi.ts (framework-free, NO React imports; import style consistent with src/lib/recommendation.ts). Export: `computeBmi(heightCm: number, weightKg: number): number` = weightKg / (m*m) where m = heightCm/100, returning NaN when heightCm/weightKg are not finite or heightCm <= 0 (guard divide-by-zero). Export a `BmiCategory` union type `"underweight" | "normal" | "overweight" | "obese"`. Export `bmiCategory(bmi: number): BmiCategory` using ASIA-PACIFIC thresholds: underweight < 18.5, normal 18.5-22.9, overweight 23-24.9, obese >= 25; decide and document in a comment what a NaN input returns (return "normal" as the safe no-op default so a transient invalid value never pushes an aggressive/strict adjustment). Export bounds constants HEIGHT_MIN_CM=100, HEIGHT_MAX_CM=250, WEIGHT_MIN_KG=30, WEIGHT_MAX_KG=300. Export a validator the UI can reuse, e.g. `isValidHeight(cm: number): boolean`, `isValidWeight(kg: number): boolean`, and a combined `isValidBmiInput(heightCm: number, weightKg: number): boolean` (finite + within inclusive bounds).

Create src/lib/__tests__/bmi.test.ts following the existing lib test style (vitest `describe`/`it`/`expect`, `@/` alias). Cover computeBmi correctness (e.g. 170cm/65kg approximately 22.49 via toBeCloseTo), invalid/zero height -> NaN; each Asia-Pacific boundary: 18.49 underweight, 18.5 normal, 22.9 normal, 23.0 overweight, 24.9 overweight, 25.0 obese; validator bounds at 100/250 cm and 30/300 kg (inclusive) plus just-outside values.

Update EVERY place a ProfilingAnswers literal is constructed so the strict compile stays green. In src/features/onboarding/OnboardingFlow.tsx both the handleConfirm `answers` literal and the inline `answers` object passed to RecommendationStep currently build ProfilingAnswers without height/weight; add draft heightCm/weightKg (introduce `const [heightCm, setHeightCm] = useState<number | null>(null)` and the same for weightKg at the top with the other draft state, and include `heightCm: heightCm as number, weightKg: weightKg as number` in both literals). FEAT-003 wires the actual BmiStep UI/gating; here only make the type satisfied so the project compiles.

Update src/lib/__tests__/recommendation.test.ts so its `answers(goal, exercises, intensity)` helper also supplies normal-BMI height/weight (e.g. heightCm: 170, weightKg: 65 => BMI ~22.5 => normal) by returning `{ goal, exercises, intensity, heightCm: 170, weightKg: 65 }`, and fix any inline ProfilingAnswers literals in that file the same way, so all existing R1-R16 rows and invariants keep their current expected outcomes (BMI is still a pure no-op until FEAT-002).
acceptance_criteria: src/types/index.ts ProfilingAnswers has required heightCm: number and weightKg: number; existing optional fields retained.
src/lib/bmi.ts exists, is React-free, and exports computeBmi, BmiCategory, bmiCategory, the four bounds constants, and the validator(s) described.
Running `npx tsc --noEmit` reports no errors (every ProfilingAnswers construction site satisfies the new required fields).
Running `npx vitest run` passes with the new bmi tests included and the pre-existing recommendation tests still green (total test count greater than 155).
findings:
DONE. tsc --noEmit clean; full suite 174 passed (was 155 baseline + 17 new bmi tests; no-emoji scan grew and stays green). BMI remains a pure no-op on recommendations (recommendMethod untouched) — FEAT-002 owns applyBmiAdjustment.

src/types/index.ts: ProfilingAnswers now has MANDATORY `heightCm: number` and `weightKg: number` (added after `intensity`, before the optional lastMealHour?/wakeHour?). Existing optionals retained.

src/lib/bmi.ts exact exports (framework-free, no React):
- `computeBmi(heightCm: number, weightKg: number): number` — returns NaN when either input is non-finite or heightCm <= 0; else weightKg / (heightCm/100)^2.
- type `BmiCategory = "underweight" | "normal" | "overweight" | "obese"`.
- `bmiCategory(bmi: number): BmiCategory` — Asia-Pacific: <18.5 underweight, 18.5-22.9 normal, 23-24.9 overweight, >=25 obese; NaN -> "normal" (safe no-op default, so a transient invalid value never triggers an aggressive/strict adjustment — FEAT-002 can rely on this).
- bounds consts: `HEIGHT_MIN_CM = 100`, `HEIGHT_MAX_CM = 250`, `WEIGHT_MIN_KG = 30`, `WEIGHT_MAX_KG = 300`.
- validators: `isValidHeight(cm: number): boolean`, `isValidWeight(kg: number): boolean`, `isValidBmiInput(heightCm: number, weightKg: number): boolean` (finite + inclusive bounds).

src/lib/__tests__/bmi.test.ts: 17 tests covering compute correctness/NaN guards, every Asia-Pacific boundary, inclusive bound edges.

OnboardingFlow.tsx (for FEAT-003): added draft state near the other drafts — `const [heightCm, setHeightCm] = useState<number | null>(null)` and `const [weightKg, setWeightKg] = useState<number | null>(null)`. Both ProfilingAnswers literals (handleConfirm `answers` and the inline object passed to RecommendationStep) now include `heightCm: heightCm as number, weightKg: weightKg as number`. TOTAL_STEPS is still 4 (FEAT-003 bumps to 5 and inserts BmiStep + wires setHeightCm/setWeightKg + gating). NOTE: setHeightCm/setWeightKg are currently unused (no UI yet); tsconfig has no noUnusedLocals so tsc is clean, but eslint may warn — FEAT-003 consumes them.

recommendation.test.ts: `answers(goal, exercises, intensity)` helper now returns `{ goal, exercises, intensity, heightCm: 170, weightKg: 65 }` (BMI ~22.5 => normal). The two inline literal sites (invariants `allInputs.push` and the degenerate-equivalence `recommendMethod({...})` pair) were given the same 170/65 so all R1-R16 rows and invariants keep their expected outcomes.
